samples.summary: `revokeInvite` return shape changed from the full deleted invite record to `{ id }`, changing the DELETE /workspaces/:id/invites/:inviteId response body
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:110 returns the service result straight to the HTTP client. Previously `prisma.workspaceInvite.delete()` returned the whole row (token, workspaceId, role, expiresAt, createdBy); it now returns `{ id: inviteId }`. The only in-repo consumer, packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:138-147 (`revokeInvite` -> Promise<void>), ignores the body, so nothing in this repo breaks — but any external/API consumer of this endpoint (it is a public REST route) sees a narrowed payload. Worth confirming no API doc/contract test asserts the old shape.

samples.summary: The self-removal ("leave workspace") path the new test now asserts leaves stale global state: it invalidates only ["workspaces", workspaceId], not the ["workspaces"] list, and does not navigate away
samples.evidence: The delta adds `lets a non-owner member remove themselves` (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-settings.test.tsx:163-177), promoting the self-leave flow to a first-class asserted behaviour. `removeMemberMutation.onSuccess` (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:134-139) invalidates only `["workspaces", workspaceId]`, which refetches `fetchWorkspace` for a workspace the user just left (now a 403 -> isError branch), and never invalidates the `["workspaces"]` list consumed by the sidebar at packages/frontend/src/app/Layout.tsx:42, so the departed workspace stays in the switcher until a reload. Contrast the delete-workspace mutation at workspace-settings.tsx:173-180, which does refetch ["workspaces"] and navigate. Fix belongs in the removeMember onSuccess handler.
